edges.limitations: Flies have no compact vertebrate myelin, so the model shows glial ensheathment failure rather than hypomyelination itself.

nodes.description: Biallelic splice-site (the recurrent IVS5+1G>T), frameshift, deletion and missense variants in HYCC1 cause complete or severe hyccin deficiency. Truncating and splice alleles give the full phenotype with peripheral neuropathy; missense alleles such as p.Leu53Pro leave some protein and a milder course.

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of hyccin, a newly identified membrane protein, causes hypomyelination and congenital cataract.
evidence.snippet: We identified mutations in five affected families, resulting in a deficiency of hyccin, a newly identified 521-amino acid membrane protein.

evidence.reference_title: Novel FAM126A mutations in hypomyelination and congenital cataract disease.
evidence.snippet: A residual amount of hyccin protein in primary fibroblasts was demonstrated by functional studies indicating that missense mutations are likely to have less detrimental effects if compared with splice-site mutations or deletions that cause the full-blown HCC phenotype, including peripheral nervous system involvement.

evidence.snippet: WES identified a novel homozygous mutation (NM_032581: c.636_639del p.C213Dfs*7) in the FAM126A gene.

nodes.description: Myelin is never adequately laid down in the central nervous system, and peripheral nerves show reduced myelinated-fibre density with thin or absent myelin sheaths. MRI shows diffuse supratentorial hypomyelination, often deep cerebellar white-matter hypomyelination, increased periventricular white-matter water content and brainstem pyramidal tract involvement; older patients add white-matter loss and gliosis.

nodes.description: Hyccin is an intrinsic component of the plasma-membrane phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase complex with PI4KIIIalpha, TTC7 and EFR3, binding TTC7 through a large interface. Its absence lowers the levels of the other subunits and so of plasma-membrane PI4-kinase activity. Hyccin itself has no catalytic activity (GO annotates it only with protein binding), so the gene is placed on this node, whose molecular function is the activity of the complex it stabilises.

nodes.description: Glial knockdown of the fly hyccin ortholog reduces glial enrichment and disrupts axonal sheaths and vision; human FAM126A or FAM126B rescues it fully and plasma-membrane-targeted PI4KIIIalpha partly, and PI4KIIIalpha knockdown phenocopies it.

nodes.description: Less PtdIns(4)P, a determinant of plasma-membrane identity and the precursor of PtdIns(4,5)P2, is made at the plasma membrane. The proposed pathogenic site is the oligodendrocyte, whose myelinating function requires massive plasma-membrane expansion; this cell-type link is proposed from the protein's expression pattern and the fly model rather than measured in human oligodendrocytes.

evidence.reference_title: The leukodystrophy protein FAM126A (hyccin) regulates PtdIns(4)P synthesis at the plasma membrane.
evidence.snippet: We propose that HCC pathogenesis involves defects in PtdIns(4)P production in oligodendrocytes, whose specialized function requires massive plasma membrane expansion and thus generation of PtdIns(4)P and downstream phosphoinositides.
